description: SAR2SAR despeckling test (via deepdespeckling package, pretrained weights, no training/Ghana-coverage dependency) on the pilot's real Sentinel-1 GRD scenes -- alternative to the Amieva/Ayala/Galar Stripmap-based super-resolution approach, which was blocked by unknown/unlikely Ghana Stripmap coverage.
methodology_note: First attempt used patch_size=64 (forced by the small 122x142 pilot raster, far below the model's intended patch_size=256) and produced visible tiling/blocking artifacts that directly contaminated the water mask (large rectangular blobs following patch seams). Corrected by despeckling on a padded extent (EXTRA_PAD_DEG=0.15, giving a 433x453 raster) at the intended patch_size=256/stride=254, then cropping back to the actual pilot bbox for comparison -- boundary effects become a small fraction of the image instead of dominating it.

results_corrected_methodology.qualitative: Despeckled water mask shows a spatially coherent connected blob (plausible real channel/floodplain feature) rather than scattered isolated pixels seen in the raw classification. A few faint residual patch-seam lines remain but no longer dominate the result.

results_flawed_methodology_patch64.note: Superseded -- kept for the record to show why the padded-extent fix mattered. Lower agreement here was partly driven by tiling artifacts, not genuine despeckling signal.

conclusion: Real, positive effect on noise within the existing resolution -- does NOT address the actual resolution ceiling (same pixel dimensions; does not help resolve sub-100m features like the Circle interchange bottleneck). Real added cost: per-scene neural network inference on a padded extent, not benchmarked at full pipeline scale (40 scenes x full pilot grid). Worth a team decision on whether the noise-reduction quality gain justifies the added pipeline complexity and runtime before adopting as a default preprocessing step.
